name: essence-language
description: Language support for Essence: syntax highlighting, diagnostics, navigation, completion and debugging.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The bundled Language Server only reads and analyses text, and diagnostics and navigation are exactly what is wanted while auditing an unfamiliar repository, so they stay on. The trust-sensitive settings are 'essence.server.path', 'essence.cli.path', 'essence.bun.path' and 'essence.node.path': each names an executable to spawn, which a workspace could point at a program it ships itself, so workspace-scoped values of them are ignored here. Debugging itself is unavailable in Restricted Mode either way — VS Code blocks debug sessions there.

scripts.build: bun run build:server && bun run build:extension

essence.server.path.markdownDescription: Use a different Language Server than the one bundled with this extension. Leave empty to use the bundled one.

essence.bun.path.markdownDescription: Where to find Bun, if the extension cannot find it on its own. Only needed when `#essence.server.path#` or `#essence.cli.path#` points at source rather than a `.js` bundle.

essence.node.path.markdownDescription: Which Node the debugger runs your programs on, if it cannot find one on its own or you want a specific version. A launch configuration's `runtimeExecutable` overrides this.

essence.inlayHints.enabled.description: Show inferred Types as inlay hints where the source states none — Constants, Variables, and the Parameters and return Type of contextually typed Function literals. It also governs the values a live test run records: the ghost text after a Constant in a test body, after a failed expect and on a § ? line.

essence.tests.enabled.description: Run the tests of the workspace as you type. Only the tests a change reaches are re-run; failures appear in Problems, and the values a run recorded appear beside the lines that produced them. Turn it off to stop the automatic runs and keep every gesture that asks for one: the Test Explorer, the Run lens and Re-run Failed Tests all still run what you ask them to.

essence.tests.skipTags.markdownDescription: Tags no run of the live session selects, as bare names — `slow`, `network`. A test carries its own tags and every enclosing suite's. Tests left out this way are reported as not run rather than as failures, and the Test Explorer still lists them.

essence.tests.coverage.markdownDescription: Count what each run reaches, and report it: lines and branches in the coverage view, the lines nothing ran marked in the gutter, and — because the language is exhaustive — every `match` arm no value took and every Case of a `choice` no test ever built, as declarations. It also lets an edit re-run only the tests that reached the changed lines, since the counters record which test touched which line. Off by default: instrumenting compiles a different bundle from the one a build produces and makes the program do more work on every keystroke. Running the tests with coverage from the Test Explorer turns it on.

essence.tests.debounce.markdownDescription: How long the live session waits after the last keystroke before it runs, in milliseconds. It sits behind the diagnostics debounce on purpose: the squiggle is what a reader wants first, and a test run is the expensive thing to be wrong about.

essence.trace.server.description: Log the traffic between VS Code and the Essence Language Server to the Essence output channel, for diagnosing problems with the server.

essence.cli.path.markdownDescription: Use a specific `essence` CLI for debugging. Leave empty to use the one installed on this machine.

program.description: The .es source file to compile and debug.

cwd.description: The working directory the program runs in.

env.description: Environment variables set for the program.

stopOnEntry.description: Pause on the first statement the program's own source wrote.

runtimeExecutable.description: The executable that runs the compiled JavaScript. Debugging requires Node — the adapter speaks its inspector protocol.

glueFrames.description: What becomes of compiler-generated stack frames: hidden entirely, or shown greyed out.

keepArtifacts.description: Keep the compiled JavaScript and its map after the session, and say where they are.

artifact.description: A precompiled bundle to debug instead of compiling 'program' — its source map must sit beside it.

tests.description: Debug tests rather than the program: 'program' is compiled with its tests section and these test ids are run. An empty array runs every test in the file.
